prompt_dump.description: A versatile data handling class for test executive applications, supporting import/export in various formats, data manipulation, metadata, and configuration-based relationships. Supports large datasets via chunked imports and partitioned Parquet exports.

development_history.instruction: Create a .NET Core class called DataBall. This class will be used by a test executive application that creates and modifies data files. It should support importing from CSV, zip/tar.gz/tar.xz (of CSV files), another DataBall, Parquet file(s), SQLite database. Also support exporting to these formats. When importing, support concatenation/merge if data already exists. Define custom columns, add/modify/remove rows/columns. Support custom metadata fields and values. The class should be an efficient in-memory data structure for data operations, useful for test and measurement applications. Iterate and improve as needed.

Add functionality to initialize a row, modify fields in this row, add new fields/columns, and commit the row with command 'Roll' (because it's a DataBall). Unmodified fields propagate from the previous row unless defined as null in the new row.

When initializing the DataBall, allow loading a config file with: Metadata fields and values; Known header row fields and their data types; Relationships - if a header column changes, reset certain other fields to null (as a type of mask). Multiple relationships can be defined, e.g., certain fields depend on others.
Detail the row builder pattern; explore Apache Arrow integration (proposal); add comprehensive unit tests.

Detail the best and most efficient data backing for this class -- it should be universal. Give a proposal and recommendations. Generate documentation files for all explained concepts (each file in a code block, formatted as markdown). Regenerate new code if this changes things.

Add integration for Polars, with proposal --- Add a DataBall operation to compact -- "bounce". Optimize loaded data and automatically partition for Best storage. Eg. We could identify any repeating columns, and remove them from the main dataframe and ADD to the metadata data frame As we add, merge, etc new files, the metadata fields should be checked and either new rows of metadata added, or adding columns to metadata, or reflowing the data as needed Implement any other optimization that should be in the bounce operation. ----- Proposal for using parquet as the data backing --- Regen all the documentation files (including proposals and details), and prompt dump.

Let's keep Microsoft dataframe backing, per your proposal I like the parking to parquet idea -- we should do that on save operation. Implement that Ensure all of this (databall) can support large datasets-- eg could be 10s of GB of data

on .Save(), which can take an optional filepath to make it a "Save As" operation, should perform the .Bounce() op, and then partition the data to parquet files on-disk.  then, we should use some kind of package to bundle the files together, but it needs to be fast and efficient.  zip?  tar? other? for the entire project we want to stick to open source (FLOSS) libraries if at all possible the DataBall filetype should be "*.ball" also the entire project should be licensed under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPL 2.0) ------ please implement the features above, and correct any behavior that may have been contrary. and let's do a new prompt dump. please also create a python script file that will create ALL of these files in a directory so that I can populate my repository easily (source files, documentation files, prompt state file, license files, etc)

current_features.core_structure: Uses Microsoft.Data.Analysis.DataFrame (Arrow-backed) for data storage. Dictionary<string, object> for metadata (constants).
import_formats: DataBall (.ball ZIP with partitioned Parquet and JSON metadata)
export_formats: DataBall (.ball ZIP with partitioned Parquet and JSON)
data_manipulation: Row builder: InitializeRow (optional initial values), ModifyField, Roll (commit with propagation and relationships)
Bounce: Compact by removing constants to metadata, deduplicate rows, optional partitioned Parquet export
current_features.config_loading: JSON config for metadata, column types (int, long, float, double, bool, datetime, string), relationships (trigger field and list of fields to reset if trigger changes)
current_features.merge_behavior: Append with schema alignment, filling nulls for missing columns. Checks metadata consistency, promotes to columns if values differ.
current_features.relationships_logic: On Roll, if trigger field changed (value differs from original or newly set), reset dependent fields to null unless explicitly modified.
current_features.save_behavior: Save(filePath=null, partitionColumns=null): Performs Bounce, saves to .ball (ZIP with metadata.json and Parquet data, partitioned if specified).

plans_and_todos.improvements: Enhance archive import/export to fully support tar.gz/tar.xz. Improve merge to handle schema differences more robustly (e.g., type coercion). Add support for multiple tables in SQLite if needed. Optimize for large datasets with lazy loading. Add querying/filtering methods on DataFrame. Enhance bounce with full normalization and auto-partition selection.
plans_and_todos.future_features: Integration with test/measurement specifics (e.g., timestamping, unit conversions). Versioning for DataBall format. Error handling enhancements. Serialization of relationships and expected types in exports if required. Potential Polars interop. Out-of-core mode with partitioned Parquet as backing.

prompt_dump.recreation_instructions: To recreate: Start with a new .NET project using Microsoft.Data.Analysis, Parquet.Net, SharpCompress, System.Text.Json, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite. Implement the class step-by-step following the development_history instructions, incorporating current_features. Use the last provided code version as a base but rebuild logically without copying verbatim. Add unit tests using xUnit. For large data, implement chunked imports and partitioned exports. License under MPL 2.0. Use ZIP for .ball files.
